claims.text: Machine-learning interatomic potentials can predict melting temperatures of refractory alloys with near-DFT accuracy.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can predict enthalpies of fusion of refractory alloys with near-DFT accuracy.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can predict entropies of fusion of refractory alloys with near-DFT accuracy.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can predict volume changes at melting for refractory alloys with near-DFT accuracy.
Machine-learning potentials offer vastly lower computational cost than direct ab initio molecular dynamics and thereby enable high-throughput screening.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can be used for extensive molecular-dynamics simulations of refractory high-entropy alloys over a wide temperature range.
The machine-learning force field should be trained on ab initio data.
Reliable melting predictions require training data that cover the relevant high-temperature phase space.
A highly accurate machine-learning interatomic potential can describe a refractory high-entropy alloy such as MoNbTaW.
Reduced computational overhead from the machine-learning potential permits the use of larger simulation cells and longer sampling times.
The machine-learning potential approximates the alloy free-energy surface with near-DFT fidelity.
Classical force-field molecular dynamics can quantitatively agree with first-principles calculations and experiments for selected structural and ordering properties of a high-entropy alloy.
Ab initio thermodynamic integration using first-principles molecular dynamics is extremely expensive for large-scale or high-throughput studies.
Machine-learning-potential reliability may degrade for compositions or temperature regimes outside the training distribution.
Periodic recalibration of the machine-learning potential may be required.
Insufficient, biased, or phase-space-incomplete training data may produce inaccurate melting-property predictions.

The method can be tested by comparing its predicted melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and melting volume change against ab initio thermodynamic-integration results for the same alloy.
A discrepancy greater than 5% between machine-learning and ab initio predictions would falsify the hypothesis.
